vocabulary.meaning_en: to officially ask a company to supply goods
vocabulary.example: I'd like to place an order for printer paper.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a request to buy goods; to ask for goods
vocabulary.example: We'll have to order more boxes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: available in the shop or store now
vocabulary.example: We don't have many green boxes in stock.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take goods to a place
vocabulary.example: They will deliver the boxes on Monday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to get something that is sent to you
vocabulary.example: When can we expect to receive them?
We expect the delivery next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: expensive and of very high quality
vocabulary.example: Each product comes in a luxury box.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a company that sells goods to other companies
vocabulary.example: I'll call our supplier and order more.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say that something is definitely true or will happen
vocabulary.example: Please phone the client to confirm the order.

vocabulary.meaning_ar: عدد لا بأس به / كثير نسبيًا
vocabulary.example: We're going to need quite a few boxes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to know someone or something because you saw or heard it before
to give a message to someone else
vocabulary.example: I'll pass that on to her.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to add someone to an email so they see it too
vocabulary.example: Please copy me in on the email.
He's your client, so you should call him.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the outer surfaces of a box
vocabulary.example: Could we have our logo on the sides of the box?

vocabulary.meaning_en: thinking about something all the time
vocabulary.example: He's obsessed with being on time.
An email is safer than a phone call for some things.

fine_lines.title: I want vs I'd like
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I want مباشرة وقد تبدو غير مهذبة مع العملاء والموردين. I'd like (= I would like) أكثر تهذيبًا عند الطلب.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I want" is direct and can sound rude in business. "I'd like" (= I would like) is the polite way to order.

examples.sentence: I'd like to place an order for some boxes, please.

fine_lines.title: receive vs deliver
fine_lines.explanation_ar: deliver يقوم بها المورّد (يوصل البضاعة)، و receive يقوم بها الزبون (يستلمها).
fine_lines.explanation_en: The supplier delivers the goods; the customer receives them.

examples.sentence: We received the order this morning.

expressions.phrase: I'd like to place an order for...
expressions.meaning_en: a polite way to start an order
expressions.example: I'd like to place an order for fifty chairs, please.

expressions.meaning_en: used to say how much you need
expressions.example: We're going to need about two hundred.

expressions.meaning_en: a polite way to add a request
expressions.example: Could we also have our company name on the boxes?

expressions.phrase: When can we expect to receive them?
expressions.meaning_en: used to ask about the delivery date
expressions.example: Thank you. When can we expect to receive them?

expressions.meaning_en: used when the person called is not available
expressions.example: She's busy at the moment. Can I take a message?

expressions.phrase: I'll pass that on to her.
expressions.meaning_en: I will give her the message
expressions.example: Thank you, I'll pass that on to her.

grammar.title: Polite requests: I'd like / Could you / Could we
grammar.explanation_ar: عند الطلب من مورّد استخدم صيغًا مهذبة: I'd like to + فعل أو I'd like + اسم، و Could you + فعل أساسي...? و Could we also have + اسم...? وأضف please.
grammar.explanation_en: When ordering, use polite forms: "I'd like to + verb" or "I'd like + noun", "Could you + base verb...?", "Could we also have + noun...?" and add "please".
examples: I'd like to place an order for paper.
Could you send it by Friday, please?
Could we also have a receipt?

grammar.title: be going to need
grammar.explanation_ar: We're going to need تعبّر عن حاجة مستقبلية مخطط لها: subject + am/is/are + going to + need.
grammar.explanation_en: "We're going to need" talks about a planned future need: subject + am/is/are + going to + need.
examples: We're going to need more boxes.
I'm going to need your help tomorrow.
They're going to need a bigger room.

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to start an order?
choices: I'd like to place an order for some boxes.
questions.explanation_ar: I'd like to place an order هي الصيغة المهذبة.
questions.explanation_en: "I'd like to place an order" is polite.

questions.question: Complete: When can we expect to ___ them?
"We don't have many in stock" means...
choices: We have only a few available
questions.explanation_en: "In stock" means available in the store.

questions.question: Complete: Could we ___ have our name on the sides?
questions.explanation_ar: Could we also have = هل يمكننا أيضًا.
questions.explanation_en: "Could we also have" adds a request.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد Could you يأتي الفعل الأساسي.
questions.explanation_en: After "Could you" use the base verb.

questions.question: Complete: We're going ___ need quite a few.
"Copy me in on the email" means...
choices: Add me so I also get the email
questions.explanation_en: It means add me so I receive it too.

questions.question: What is the opposite of "in stock"?
"I'll pass that on to her" means...
questions.explanation_en: "Pass on" means give the message to her.
